summary: Donald R. Davis Jr. specializes in Indology and religious studies, having studied under Patrick Olivelle, Ludo Rocher, and Richard W. Lariviere. He served as Associate Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2006–2012) and is on the faculty at UT Austin (attested 2026).

Donald S. Lopez Jr. is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his BA and PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, held a post at Middlebury College (1986), and became a Distinguished University Professor at the University of Michigan in 1990.
Dondub Buddhayin was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who served as Abbot of Ganden Dargye Ling (attested 1933) and of Chilttai Monastery. He also taught Eugène Obermiller.

id: P:Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso
summary: Dong Kam Tulku Ngawang Damchö Gyatso studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Dongak Chokyi Nyima studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Dongak Tendzin studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, while also teaching both Khyentse Wangpo and Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye as well as Shechen Gyaltsab.

Dongchu (1908–1977) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Minnan Buddhist Institute and under Taixu, Aiting, and Nanting. He served as dean of Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy (~1944–1949) and abbot of Dinghui Monastery (~1945–1949).

Donna C. Kurtz is an archaeologist and historian who earned degrees from the University of Cincinnati (BA), Yale University (MA), and Somerville College, Oxford (DPhil 1965–1968). She held posts at the University of Oxford and the Classical Art Research Centre (~1970–2011).

Donna Lynn Brown works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned an MA and PhD at the University of Manitoba, an MDiv from Maitripa College, and served as a sessional instructor at the University of Manitoba in 2023.
Donna Strahan is a specialist in history and archaeology who served as a conservator at the Metropolitan Museum of Art (attested 2010) and became Head at the National Museum of Asian Art in 2014.
Dor Bahadur Bista, working in Tibetology and other fields, studied at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus. He served as a professor at Tribhuvan University (~1975–1990) and founded the Karnali Institute.
Doranne Jacobson is a scholar in Indology and anthropology who earned her doctorate at Columbia University, where she also served as a seminar associate at the Southern Asian Institute.

Doris Meth Srinivasan specializes in Indology, religious studies, and art history. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, was a curator at the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art (~1993–2000), and is a Research Scholar at Stony Brook University.
Doris Unterthurner is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed her MA at the University of Vienna under the supervision of Klaus-Dieter Mathes.
Dorje Rinchen (1819–1867) was an active figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Sakya Yab Jé Kün Ga Rinchen and several other masters, and later taught Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dorje Tseten (1925–2013) was a scholar of Tibetology and history who studied education at Beijing Normal University (~1944–1948) and served as director of the China Tibetology Research Center from 1986 to 2000.

Dorji Banzarov (1822–1855) worked in linguistics, religious studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his education and doctoral dissertation at Kazan Imperial University (~1842–1846) under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski.

Dorji Penjore, working in Tibetology and history, earned a PhD in anthropology from the Australian National University (2012–2016). He served as Chief Researcher at the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH (2017–2021) and joined the Royal Institute of Management in 2021.

Dorji Wangchuk is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and David P. Jackson. He has taught at the University of Hamburg since 1998, becoming Professor in 2009.

Dorothy C. Wong works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She earned degrees from International Christian University, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, and Harvard University (PhD 1995), and is an affiliate faculty member at the University of Virginia (attested 2026).
